drafted_from: The tool's source and local fixture tests. Public repository bundles were checked by the source command, but this tool has not yet been proved through an installed Workshop row; the example below is illustrative, not an installed run.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep the public repository https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World as one text file. Tell me its commit, licence, file identity, and every file left out. Do not run any repository code."
no_lists_because: This tool reads a public repository and keeps one local text file. It reads and writes no account list or database row.
instructions: 1. Give your AI the public repository's https address. If you need a particular branch, tag or commit, give its ref too.
2. Have the AI discover tool:keep-a-repository-as-text, read its schema, then run it with the address and optional ref. It runs on your computer and does not install or execute repository code.

3. Read the answer: the commit and licence, the bundle_path, bundle_bytes and bundle_blake3, files_kept, and files_skipped with each reason. A missing repository or ref gives an error instead of a bundle.

4. Read the text bundle at bundle_path. A skipped file is not covered by the bundle. A licence in a subfolder does not license the entire repository; keep the scope the answer names. Keep the original bundle unchanged when passing it to your library's owner.

worked_examples.title: Keep a public repository as text without running it
worked_examples.ask: Keep https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World as a text bundle and report anything left out.
worked_examples.given: Illustrative input only. The installed tool still needs a real fixture run before this kit's draft mark can be removed.
worked_examples.hands_back: The local fixture tests keep 3 text files and list picture.bin as binary, huge.txt as over the per-file cap, and link-to-readme as a symbolic link. An installed Workshop result for the example address has not been observed.
